page: Microsoft Azure D96pds_v6 is a general-purpose virtual machine belonging to the Dpdsv6 family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It is powered by a dedicated ARM64 Microsoft Neoverse-N2 processor featuring 96 physical cores and 96 vCPUs operating at 3.4 GHz. The hardware configuration includes 384.0 GB of system memory, providing a balanced 4.0 GB of RAM per core. For local storage, the instance is equipped with a 5669 GB local NVMe SSD, and it supports Premium Storage. No GPUs are included in this configuration.

Performance benchmarks indicate top-tier multi-core execution and memory subsystem capabilities. The server achieves top-tier results in multi-core stress-ng CPU performance, multi-threaded bzip3 decompression, and Geekbench multi-core tests, including software compilation with Clang. Memory bandwidth is highly efficient, scoring in the top tier for both cached small-block read operations and large-block read/write operations. Database operations and Redis SET operations also rank in the top tier, alongside static web serving throughput. Single-core performance, such as single-threaded gzip compression and Geekbench single-core scores, falls into the average to strong categories.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the D96pds_v6 offers high resource density and a balanced vCPU-to-RAM ratio, leveraging the power efficiency of the ARM64 architecture to deliver high multi-threaded throughput without the premium cost of specialized compute-optimized hardware. The presence of a large 5669 GB local NVMe SSD makes it highly suitable for data-intensive applications. This server is recommended for multi-threaded workloads, database hosting, high-throughput Redis deployments, static web serving, software compilation, and medium-to-large scale LLM inference text generation.
